rationale:
Decision: split any_radius_gr_height_transfer into 2 children. The node is at depth 3, so the children are at depth 4 (limit 6).

WHY SPLIT
- A leaf adds only its single theorem. Unsplit, steps 0-7 become one declaration mixing three kinds of work:
  - a measure-theoretic null-set transport (steps 1, 3, 6 and the last bullet of step 7);
  - a pointwise linear-algebra estimate at one graph point (steps 4-5);
  - the integration chain (step 7).
- The first two are self-contained general obligations. The integration chain stays in the parent.
  - ae_transfer: if F is nu-a.e.-measurable and the integral of h(F(x)) d nu is at most the integral of h d mu for every Borel h >= 0, then the same holds for every mu-a.e.-measurable g. It holds for arbitrary nu, mu, F, g. It is the reusable form of the E1 null-set argument; campanato_input has the same E1 pattern.
  - pointwise_height: |b - Ax|^2/|x|^(n+2) <= 2^(n+4) |Y - PY|^2/|Y|^(n+2) at Y = q(graphPoint(x, b)), when ||A|| <= 1/7 and |b| <= |x|/7. P is any linear map that fixes q(graphPoint(x, Ax)) (H1) and satisfies the normal bound (H2).
- Neither child restates the parent or another DAG node.
- Leaving the node unsplit would also work (about 185 Lean lines). The split isolates the two independent difficulties into short leaves and leaves an assembly of about 80 lines:
  - lower integrals of possibly non-Borel integrands;
  - the power/ratio algebra.
- Grandchildren see only the frozen contract plus their declared siblings (as recorded in graph_rate's decomposition-v2). Therefore:
  - pointwise_height takes (P1) at x and (P2) as its hypotheses (H1), (H2). With P := P_{Du(x)} they are syntactically plane_projections' first two conjuncts.
  - It re-derives the two coordinate identities it needs: (G1) = (L1) and (G4) = (L4).
  - Every application of la_basics and plane_projections stays in the parent.
- The two children do not depend on each other, so the dependency graph is acyclic.

PARENT ASSEMBLY
This assembly replaces the p~ route of supplied steps 1, 3, 5 and 6; the parent prover should not construct p~.
Notation:
- Omega := ball 0 R;
- F(x) := q(graphPoint(x, u x));
- S := q '' graphOver u Omega;
- G0(y) := ofReal(|y - p_y y|^2/|y|^(n+2)), the right-hand integrand.
Steps:
1. (Supplied step 2.) la_basics (L1), (L3) make (a, c) -> graphPoint(a, c) linear on the finite-dimensional R^n x R^l, hence continuous (LinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional). u is continuous on Omega (ContDiffOn.continuousOn) and q is continuous. So F is continuous on Omega, and AEMeasurable F (volume.restrict Omega) holds (ContinuousOn.aemeasurable, Omega open).
2. (Supplied step 6, for p itself.)
   - y -> (p_y, y) is a.e.-strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.prodMk), and (M, v) -> M v is continuous (Continuous.clm_apply). So y -> p_y y is a.e.-strongly measurable.
   - Then sub, norm, pow_const, div and ennreal_ofReal give AEMeasurable G0 V.weight, hence also for V.weight.restrict S.
3. (Supplied step 4.) Let x be in Omega. Then 0 is in Omega, and u is differentiable on the convex open ball (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn). Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le with u(0) = 0 gives |u x| <= |x|/7.
4. (Supplied step 5.) Filter (E2) together with ae_restrict_mem. At such x:
   - rewrite p_{F(x)} as P_{Du(x)};
   - apply pointwise_height with P := P_{Du(x)}, A := Du(x), b := u(x);
   - its hypotheses are ||Du(x)|| <= 1/7, item 3, (H1) := (P1) at (Du(x), x), and (H2) := (P2) at Du(x);
   - ofReal_le_ofReal and ofReal_mul (with 2^(n+4) >= 0) give ofReal(|u x - Du(x)x|^2/|x|^(n+2)) <= ofReal(2^(n+4)) G0(F(x)) for a.e. x in Omega.
5. (Supplied step 7.)
   - Apply lintegral_mono_ae, then lintegral_const_mul' (ofReal is never infinite).
   - Apply ae_transfer with nu := volume.restrict Omega, mu := V.weight.restrict S, this F, the (E1_Omega) hypothesis verbatim, and g := G0 (item 2).
   - Finish with lintegral_mono_set, using S contained in ball 0 rho.
Correspondence with the supplied proof:
- Supplied steps 1 and 3 and the last bullet of step 7 (Borel representative, null set transported along F, a.e. replacement) are exactly ae_transfer's proof. It is applied to a Borel version of G0 instead of to p~, so step 5 can use p_{F(x)} directly from (E2).
- Step 0 needs no separate case. If R <= 0, Omega is empty and every a.e. statement on it is vacuous; otherwise 0 is in Omega whenever some x is.

NOT ANOTHER DAG NODE
- No DAG lean_statement equals either child type. The closest are anyrad_gc_graph_lintegral_transfer and campanato_input; they have different shapes and sit in other subtrees.
- The names any_radius_gr_ht_ae_transfer and any_radius_gr_ht_pointwise_height appear nowhere:
  - not among the 555 lean_name fields in dag.json and nodes/*/*.json;
  - in no snapshot project file;
  - in no .lean file on any of 683 distinct git ref tips.

subproblems.title: Push-forward domination by Borel integrands extends to a.e.-measurable integrands (null-set transport; steps 1, 3, 7 of the height transfer)
subproblems.statement: Let n, l >= 0. Let nu be a measure on R^n (Rn n) and mu a measure on R^(n+l) (Amb n l), both spaces with their Borel sigma-algebras, and let F : R^n -> R^(n+l) be nu-a.e.-measurable (AEMeasurable F nu). Assume (E): for every Borel measurable h : R^(n+l) -> [0, infinity], the lower Lebesgue integral of h(F(x)) d nu(x) is at most the lower Lebesgue integral of h d mu. Then for every g : R^(n+l) -> [0, infinity] that is mu-a.e.-measurable (AEMeasurable g mu), the lower integral of g(F(x)) d nu(x) is at most the lower integral of g d mu. (Lower integrals are Mathlib's lintegral, defined for arbitrary [0, infinity]-valued functions.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Rn n)) (μ : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (F : Rn n → Amb n ℓ), AEMeasurable F ν → (∀ g : Amb n ℓ → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g → ∫⁻ x, g (F x) ∂ν ≤ ∫⁻ y, g y ∂μ) → ∀ g : Amb n ℓ → ℝ≥0∞, AEMeasurable g μ → ∫⁻ x, g (F x) ∂ν ≤ ∫⁻ y, g y ∂μ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation. nu is a measure on R^n = Rn n and mu a measure on R^(n+l) = Amb n l, each with its Borel sigma-algebra; F : R^n -> R^(n+l) is nu-a.e.-measurable. All integrals are lower Lebesgue integrals (Mathlib lintegral) of [0, infinity]-valued functions. They are defined for arbitrary functions and do not change when the integrand is changed on a null set (lintegral_congr_ae). (E) is the hypothesis: the integral of h(F(x)) d nu(x) is at most the integral of h d mu, for every Borel h : R^(n+l) -> [0, infinity]. The argument transports a mu-null set along F and then replaces g by a Borel version.

Fix g : R^(n+l) -> [0, infinity] that is mu-a.e.-measurable.

1. Borel version. By definition of a.e.-measurability there is a Borel measurable g~ : R^(n+l) -> [0, infinity] with g = g~ mu-a.e. (AEMeasurable.mk, AEMeasurable.measurable_mk, AEMeasurable.ae_eq_mk). Let N := {y : g(y) != g~(y)}. Then mu(N) = 0 (ae_iff).

2. Measurable hull. Let N' := toMeasurable mu N. Then N' is a measurable set, N is contained in N', and mu(N') = mu(N) = 0 (measurableSet_toMeasurable, subset_toMeasurable, measure_toMeasurable).

3. Transport of the null set. The indicator 1_{N'} (1 on N', 0 elsewhere) is Borel measurable because N' is measurable (Measurable.indicator). By (E) with h := 1_{N'} and lintegral_indicator_one:
integral of 1_{N'}(F(x)) d nu(x) <= integral of 1_{N'} d mu = mu(N') = 0.
Lower integrals are >= 0, so the integral of 1_{N'}(F(x)) d nu(x) equals 0.

4. The function x -> 1_{N'}(F(x)) is the Borel function 1_{N'} composed with the nu-a.e.-measurable F, hence nu-a.e.-measurable (Measurable.comp_aemeasurable). A [0, infinity]-valued nu-a.e.-measurable function with zero lower integral vanishes nu-a.e. (lintegral_eq_zero_iff'). Hence 1_{N'}(F(x)) = 0, i.e. F(x) is not in N', for nu-a.e. x.

5. For every such x, F(x) is not in N, because N is contained in N'. By the definition of N this means g(F(x)) = g~(F(x)). So g o F = g~ o F nu-a.e.

6. Conclusion. Use step 5 with lintegral_congr_ae, then (E) for the Borel function h := g~, then g~ = g mu-a.e. (step 1) with lintegral_congr_ae:
integral of g(F(x)) d nu(x) = integral of g~(F(x)) d nu(x) <= integral of g~ d mu = integral of g d mu.
This holds for every mu-a.e.-measurable g, which is the claim.
proof_key_steps: Borel version g~ of g with mu{g != g~} = 0, and a measurable hull N' of {g != g~} with mu(N') = 0
(E) at the Borel indicator 1_{N'} gives: integral of 1_{N'}(F(x)) d nu <= mu(N') = 0
x -> 1_{N'}(F(x)) is nu-a.e.-measurable, so F(x) is not in N' for nu-a.e. x; hence g o F = g~ o F nu-a.e.
integral of g o F d nu = integral of g~ o F d nu <= integral of g~ d mu = integral of g d mu

subproblems.title: Pointwise conical height bound at a graph point of small slope (steps 4-5 of the height transfer)
subproblems.statement: Let n, l >= 0 and write graphPoint(a, c) for the point of R^(n+l) = Amb n l whose first n coordinates are those of a in R^n and whose last l coordinates are those of c in R^l. Let q be a linear isometric equivalence of R^(n+l), P : R^(n+l) -> R^(n+l) a continuous linear map, A : R^n -> R^l a continuous linear map with operator norm ||A|| <= 1/7, x in R^n and b in R^l with |b| <= |x|/7. Assume (H1) P(q(graphPoint(x, A x))) = q(graphPoint(x, A x)); (H2) |w| <= (1 + ||A||^2)^(1/2) |q(graphPoint(0, w)) - P(q(graphPoint(0, w)))| for every w in R^l. Put Y := q(graphPoint(x, b)). Then |b - A x|^2 / |x|^(n+2) <= 2^(n+4) (|Y - P Y|^2 / |Y|^(n+2)), where real division by 0 gives 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (P : Amb n ℓ →L[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) (x : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), ‖A‖ ≤ 1 / 7 → ‖b‖ ≤ ‖x‖ / 7 → P (q (graphPoint x (A x))) = q (graphPoint x (A x)) → (∀ w : Rn ℓ, ‖w‖ ≤ Real.sqrt (1 + ‖A‖ ^ 2) * ‖q (graphPoint (0 : Rn n) w) - P (q (graphPoint (0 : Rn n) w))‖) → ‖b - A x‖ ^ 2 / ‖x‖ ^ (n + 2) ≤ 2 ^ (n + 4) * (‖q (graphPoint x b) - P (q (graphPoint x b))‖ ^ 2 / ‖q (graphPoint x b)‖ ^ (n + 2))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation. N := n + l, so Amb n l = R^N. For a in R^n and c in R^l, graphPoint(a, c) = toLp(Fin.append a c): its coordinate at Fin.castAdd l i is a_i (i < n), and its coordinate at Fin.natAdd n j is c_j (j < l). Every index of Fin N has exactly one of these two forms (Fin.addCases). |.| is the Euclidean norm and ||A|| the operator norm. q is linear with |q z| = |z|, and P is linear. Real division by 0 gives 0.
The two coordinate identities (G1), (G4) are proved below from the definition of graphPoint; the projection properties are exactly the hypotheses (H1), (H2).

1. (G1) For all a, a' in R^n and c, c' in R^l: graphPoint(a + a', c + c') = graphPoint(a, c) + graphPoint(a', c'). Compare coordinates: at castAdd l i both sides equal a_i + a'_i, and at natAdd n j both equal c_j + c'_j.

2. (G4) For all a in R^n and c in R^l: |graphPoint(a, c)|^2 = |a|^2 + |c|^2. In each Euclidean space |z|^2 = sum_k |z_k|^2 = sum_k z_k^2 (EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq; for real coordinates |z_k|^2 = z_k^2). Split the sum over Fin (n + l) into its castAdd and natAdd parts (Fin.sum_univ_add): sum_i a_i^2 + sum_j c_j^2 = |a|^2 + |c|^2.

3. Let Y := q(graphPoint(x, b)) and RHS := 2^(n+4) (|Y - P Y|^2 / |Y|^(n+2)). We have 2^(n+4) > 0, |Y - P Y|^2 >= 0 and |Y|^(n+2) >= 0. A nonnegative real divided by a nonnegative real is >= 0 (it is 0 if the denominator is 0). So RHS >= 0.

4. Case x = 0. Then |x|^(n+2) = 0^(n+2) = 0 because n + 2 >= 1. So the left side is |b - A x|^2 / 0 = 0 <= RHS by step 3.

5. Case x != 0, so |x| > 0. Put w := b - A x, T := q(graphPoint(x, A x)) and y_w := q(graphPoint(0, w)).
(a) Decomposition. Since x + 0 = x and A x + w = b, (G1) gives graphPoint(x, b) = graphPoint(x, A x) + graphPoint(0, w). Applying the linear map q: Y = T + y_w.
(b) Residual. By linearity of P and (H1), P Y = P T + P y_w = T + P y_w. Hence Y - P Y = y_w - P y_w.
(c) Normal bound. Since 0 <= ||A|| <= 1/7, we have 1 + ||A||^2 <= 1 + 1/49 <= 4 = 2^2, so (1 + ||A||^2)^(1/2) <= 2 (Real.sqrt_le_left). By (H2) for this w and by (b):
|w| <= (1 + ||A||^2)^(1/2) |y_w - P y_w| <= 2 |y_w - P y_w| = 2 |Y - P Y|.
Both sides are >= 0, so squaring gives |w|^2 <= (2 |Y - P Y|)^2 = 4 |Y - P Y|^2.
(d) Size of Y. q is an isometry, so |Y| = |graphPoint(x, b)|, and by (G4) |Y|^2 = |x|^2 + |b|^2.
- Since |b|^2 >= 0, |x|^2 <= |Y|^2. As |x| >= 0 and |Y| >= 0, this gives |x| <= |Y| (sq_le_sq₀). In particular |Y| > 0.
- Since 0 <= |b| <= |x|/7, |b|^2 <= |x|^2/49. So |Y|^2 <= (50/49)|x|^2 <= 4|x|^2 = (2|x|)^2. As |Y| >= 0 and 2|x| >= 0, this gives |Y| <= 2|x|.
(e) Powers. Let k := n + 2. From 0 <= |Y| <= 2|x|: |Y|^k <= (2|x|)^k = 2^k |x|^k (pow_le_pow_left₀, mul_pow). Also |x|^k > 0 and |Y|^k > 0.
(f) Combination. Since |x|^k > 0, the claim |w|^2 / |x|^k <= RHS is equivalent to |w|^2 <= RHS * |x|^k (div_le_iff₀). The chain below uses (c), then |Y|^k > 0, then (e) together with 4|Y - P Y|^2 / |Y|^k >= 0, and finally 4 * 2^k = 2^(n+4):
|w|^2 <= 4|Y - P Y|^2 = (4|Y - P Y|^2 / |Y|^k) |Y|^k <= (4|Y - P Y|^2 / |Y|^k)(2^k |x|^k) = 2^(n+4) (|Y - P Y|^2 / |Y|^k) |x|^k = RHS * |x|^k.
Since w = b - A x, this is the claim.

6. Steps 4 and 5 cover every x. This proves the statement for all n, l, q, P, A, x and b satisfying the hypotheses.
proof_key_steps: Coordinate identities: (G1) additivity of graphPoint and (G4) |graphPoint(a, c)|^2 = |a|^2 + |c|^2
x = 0: |x|^(n+2) = 0, so the left side is 0 <= RHS
x != 0: Y = q(graphPoint(x, A x)) + q(graphPoint(0, w)) with w = b - A x, and (H1) gives Y - P Y = y_w - P y_w
